info.bio:
Mark Lanegan (nacido el 25 de noviembre de 1964 en Ellensburg, Washington) fue un compositor y cantante conocido principalmente por su considerable éxito como solista y por haber formado parte de grupos como Screaming Trees y colaborar en grupos como Queens of the Stone Age o Mad Season.

En el año 1985, Lanegan decide formar una banda junto con los hermanos Conner, llamada Screaming Trees por el nombre de un pedal de distorsión para guitarra eléctrica.

scenes.name: Cantautores lo-fi de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Los noventa son la década del cantautor: la tecnología y las redes informales del post-punk favorecen la carrera en solitario, con Joni Mitchell y Leonard Cohen (no Dylan ni Springsteen) como maestros. El folk sombrío inaugurado por Chris Isaak, Smog y American Music Club se convierte casi en un género: Vic Chesnutt, Mark Lanegan, Mountain Goats, Elliott Smith, Jeff Buckley, Ron Sexsmith, Mike Johnson, Simon Joyner, Songs:Ohia. El neo-pop de Stephen Merritt (Magnetic Fields: Holiday, The Charm Of The Highway Strip, 69 Love Songs), Chris Connelly, Frank Black, Mike Gira (Body Lovers, Angels Of Light), Richard Davies y Eric Matthews (Cardinal), David Gray. El neo-folk de Beck (folk para la era del hip hop), John Frusciante, Sparklehorse, Bright Eyes, Rufus Wainwright, Grandaddy, Bobby Conn; el neo-country de Richard Buckner y Freedy Johnston; Steve Wynn, Mike Watt, Paul Westerberg, Ben Harper.

podcast.title: Achieving Sobriety by 2020
podcast.body: By the year 2020, Mark Lanegan had successfully become clean and sober from his addictions. "But by 2020 he was clean and sober."

podcast.title: "Devil in a Coma" Memoir
podcast.body: One of Mark Lanegan's notable books, "Devil in a Coma," details his harrowing near-death experience with COVID-19, during which he was in a coma for weeks, left temporarily deaf, and unable to walk. "One of his best is Devil in a coma, which detailed his horrible near death experience from COVID-19 when he was left temporarily deaf and unable to walk. He was in a coma for weeks."

podcast.title: Assistance from Duff McKagan
podcast.body: Duff McKagan of Guns N' Roses provided Mark Lanegan with a job as a housekeeper, offering him a place to live during a difficult period. "And he was given a job as the housekeeper for Duff McKagan of Guns and Roses just so he had some place to live."

podcast.body: For a period, Mark Lanegan earned money by painting sets for television shows. "He made money from painting sets for TV shows for a while."

podcast.title: Friendships with Notable Musicians and Figures
podcast.body: Mark Lanegan was close friends with Chef Anthony Bourdain, for whom he wrote an obituary, as well as Layne Staley of Alice in Chains, Eddie Vedder, the members of Soundgarden, and Kurt Cobain. "He was also good friends with Chef Anthony Bourdain. He wrote an obituary on Bourdain when he died. He was also buddies with doomed Ellison Chainsinger, Lane Staley. Other friends included Eddie Vedder, all the guys in Soundgarden and Kurt Cobain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Health Deterioration and Death
podcast.body: Although he survived his severe COVID-19 battle, the illness took a heavy toll on his 57-year-old body, which had been previously damaged by years of heroin and alcohol addiction, leading him to move to Killarney, Ireland, for recovery, where he eventually died at his home on February 22nd. "He was able to survive that. But it took its toll on his 57 year old body which had been abused by years of heroin and alcohol addiction. He moved to Kalarni in Ireland to recover further from COVID. But then he died at his home on February 22nd."

podcast.title: Homelessness and Rehab Efforts
podcast.body: Lanegan experienced homelessness and underwent rehabilitation multiple times, with one stint notably funded by Courtney Love. "He was homeless for a while, tried rehab a couple of times. One stint was paid for by Courtney Love."

podcast.title: Kyuss Fan and Collaborator
podcast.body: Mark Lanegan, the singer for the Screaming Trees, was a fan of Kyuss and later recruited Josh Homme to tour as his guitarist for two years. "Mark Lannigan, the singer for the screaming trees, a terribly underrated Seattle band. Mark was a fan of Kaya's and needed someone to tour with the trees and ask Josh if he would like to be his guitarist."

podcast.title: Offered Queens of the Stone Age Lead Singer Role
podcast.body: Lanegan was offered the position of lead singer for Josh Homme's new project, Queens of the Stone Age, but declined due to being too busy at the time. "Mark Lannigan was supposed to be the only other permanent person. He was offered the lead singer's spot, but he was way too busy, so he politely begged off."

podcast.body: Mark Lanegan was a highly regarded singer and songwriter who emerged from the grunge era of the 1990s. "Mark Lennigan was one of the great singers and songwriters to come out of the whole grunge era of the 1990s."

podcast.title: Struggles with Drug Addiction
podcast.body: Mark Lanegan battled severe heroin addiction, which was so extreme that he nearly required an arm amputation in 1992 due to a severe infection from injecting drugs. "But Mark always had his demons. This is a guy who shot up so much heroin that he almost had an arm amputated in 1992 because it had become so badly infected."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

podcast.title: Undisclosed Cause of Death
podcast.body: No official cause of death was released for Mark Lanegan, but his passing was not entirely unexpected given his challenging life and severe COVID-19 experience. "No cause of death was ever released, but let's just say that given his hard life in the terrible time he had with COVID, it really wasn't much of a shock."

xref.title: Josh Homme as Sole Member (Early 2004)
xref.body: In early 2004, following the firing of Nick Oliveri and the departure of Mark Lanegan, Josh Homme became the only remaining member of Queens of the Stone Age. He continued the band, given his primary role in writing 90% of the music and serving as the lead singer. "So this meant that in early 2004, Queen of the Stone Age was down to just one member, Josh Hommie."

xref.title: Screaming Trees Tour as Guitarist
xref.body: Josh Homme spent two years touring as the rhythm guitarist for the Seattle band Screaming Trees after meeting their singer Mark Lanegan, a Kyuss fan. He was described as a six-foot-five red-haired rhythm guitarist during their Lollapalooza 1996 set. "Mark was a fan of Kaya's and needed someone to tour with the trees and ask Josh if he would like to be his guitarist. So he did that for two years. If you were at Lollapalooza in 1996 and saw the tree set, that six foot five red-haired rhythm guitarist was Josh Hommie."
